strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation with detailed ablations on both LoCoMo and HotpotQA benchmarks, including robustness testing against hallucination
Substantial improvements on primary benchmark (LoCoMo): 54.17% F1 vs 45.31% GAM baseline, representing ~9% absolute improvement
Clear architectural design with intuitive master-assistant hierarchy and multi-pathway routing mechanism, well-illustrated in figures
Honest acknowledgment of latency-fidelity trade-off in limitations section and discussion of future hybrid approaches
Good implementation transparency with detailed prompts, algorithms, and case studies provided in appendices
weaknesses: Core technical novelty is limited: the central contribution ('preserve full context instead of compressing') is straightforward; 'Episodic Context Reconstruction' is poorly formalized and Equation 6 shows this is simply standard inference over full context

Critical missing ablation: no comparison of E-mem against simply providing full uncompressed context to master agent directly, making it unclear whether the multi-agent structure provides genuine advantage

Severe latency-fidelity trade-off inadequately addressed: Table 7 shows ~10x slowdown (49.74s vs 5.13s for LightMem), yet dismissed as acceptable; this severely limits practical applicability for interactive agent systems despite motivation in Section 1

Inconsistent gains across tasks and datasets: E-mem performs worse than GAM on Open Domain subset (24.89% vs 26.03%), and margins shrink significantly on larger-scale HotpotQA (55.76% vs 53.71% at 1600 docs for GPT-4o-mini), suggesting dataset-specific optimization rather than general improvement

Problematic cost analysis: Table 6 uses arbitrary 1:10 cost ratio (unsubstantiated and varies by deployment scenario); actual cost savings depend heavily on model pricing; hidden costs of summary generation not accounted for; 43× cost reduction claim is misleading without realistic pricing

Architectural comparison fairness issues: E-mem uses parallel assistant agents (additional compute) while baselines may not use equivalent multi-agent structure, making it not apples-to-apples comparison
No statistical significance testing: no confidence intervals, error bars, or multiple runs reported; no human evaluation despite claims about 'deep reasoning' and 'logical integrity'

Limited evaluation scope: only two benchmarks tested; BLEU-1 is inappropriate metric for semantic evaluation; Open Domain task failure mode not investigated; no ablation on iterative reasoning mode claimed in Section 3.4

strengths: Strong empirical results with 7.75% improvement over state-of-the-art GAM baseline on LoCoMo (54.17% vs 45.31% F1), and 6.71% improvement on HotpotQA-400 (61.46% vs 54.75%)

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation including two benchmarks, seven competing baselines (2024-2025), extensive ablation studies, hallucination robustness analysis, and cost-effectiveness validation (43× reduction vs long-context methods)
Well-motivated problem formulation with clear articulation of 'destructive de-contextualization' in existing systems, grounded in cognitive science theory of episodic memory
Elegant heterogeneous master-assistant architecture that decouples high-level planning from memory retention while maintaining uncompressed episodic contexts
Multi-pathway routing mechanism (global alignment, semantic association, symbolic trigger) is orthogonal and complementary, with ablation evidence showing each component's importance
Thorough treatment of trade-offs with honest acknowledgment of latency concerns and appropriate scoping to high-precision domains (legal, medical, scientific)
Strong reproducibility foundation: detailed algorithms, formal notation, complete system prompts, implementation details, and comprehensive appendices
Nuanced empirical insights: information saturation analysis, task-dependent model size optimization (4B for factual retrieval vs 8-14B for multi-hop reasoning), and diminishing returns at k=8 chunks
O(1) incremental streaming updates and practical cost analysis using conservative token ratio assumptions
Clear visual presentation with informative diagrams and case study demonstrating failure modes of vector retrieval approaches
weaknesses: Latency overhead remains significant in practice: reasoning phase is ~50% slower than GAM (18.72s vs 12.43s on HotpotQA-400), with total system latency of 49.74s, limiting applicability to truly interactive settings despite 'System 2 reasoning' justification

Limited technical novelty: sliding window segmentation, dense+sparse retrieval (BM25), and master-agent coordination are all conventional; main contribution is engineering integration rather than fundamental innovation
Routing mechanism specification incomplete: union of activation paths (Eq. 5) lacks clear weighted combination rules, deduplication strategy, and conflict resolution procedures
Experimental rigor gaps: no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals, single runs reported, and no error bars despite comparing against multiple methods
Limited benchmark diversity: only two datasets (LoCoMo very recent 2024, HotpotQA adapted artificially to streaming setting), both potentially favorable to the proposed approach
Scalability analysis incomplete: no evaluation on 100K+ archived contexts, unquantified storage requirements for maintaining uncompressed memories, and unclear performance degradation at scale

Fairness of baseline comparisons unclear: identical master LLM and retrieval round constraints assumed but not verified; unclear if baselines equally optimized for accuracy vs speed; long-context baseline appears relatively weak
Missing failure mode analysis: no systematic investigation of when/why E-mem underperforms, query complexity analysis, or characterization of tasks where latency overhead is unjustifiable

Design choice justifications incomplete: why 4B-8B for assistants?, no ablation on routing pathway weights, overlap strategy δ=L-S not compared to alternatives, no exploration of assistant model diversity
Hallucination evaluation limited: Table 3 reports F1 on adversarial subset but not direct hallucination metrics like false positive rate; doesn't measure actual fabrication frequency
Cost model assumptions conservative (1:10 small:large token ratio) with actual provider pricing varying significantly; real cost savings may differ
Statistical methodology gaps: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or discussion of run-to-run variance across multiple executions
Incomplete related work engagement: limited comparison with hierarchical retrieval systems (RAPTOR, ColBERT), efficient long-context methods (RoPE, Yarn), and multi-agent reasoning frameworks
Theoretical grounding weak: 'destructive de-contextualization' claim not formally proven; no theoretical analysis of when/why episodic reconstruction should outperform compression

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing destructive de-contextualization in preprocessing-based memory systems
Solid technical architecture with sensible master-assistant decoupling and multi-pathway routing mechanism
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablation studies on two main benchmarks plus additional tests
Strong improvements on complex multi-hop reasoning tasks (e.g., +10 F1 on Qwen, +8.56% multi-hop gains)
Significant cost efficiency gains (43× reduction in token costs) via computational offloading to SLMs
Transparent reproducibility effort with detailed algorithms, prompts, and implementation details in appendices
Honest acknowledgment of latency-fidelity trade-off and limitations discussion
weaknesses: Critical practical limitation: 25-70× latency overhead (10.97s vs 0.15-0.44s on HotpotQA) severely limits real-world applicability; latency issue understated in main text relative to importance
Mixed empirical results across benchmarks: HotpotQA improvements over RAG are modest (1-7%); single-hop tasks sometimes degrade; Appendix D shows underperformance vs GPT-5.1

Moderate novelty: individual components (multi-agent systems, multi-source routing, context preservation) are conventional; claimed 'episodic context reconstruction' is primarily engineering (don't preprocess) rather than fundamental advance

Limited evaluation scope: restricted to conversational QA tasks in main evaluation; 'System 2 reasoning' claim overstated for information retrieval; AMA benchmark with strong results relegated to appendix
Routing mechanism underspecified: weight selection (w₁, w₂, w₃) unjustified; threshold determination lacks ablation; scalability to millions of documents unclear
Scalability concerns inadequately addressed: storage claims conservative (30KB per agent optimistic); VRAM overhead with concurrent agents not fully analyzed; no maximum archive size discussion

Comparison fairness issues: heterogeneous compute strategy (SLM+large model) differs from baselines; some baselines perform surprisingly poorly (A-mem 39.65 vs RAG 44.73); cost model conservative but actual pricing varies
Incomplete technical justification: temporal anchoring mechanism described but not empirically validated; evidence aggregation strategy underspecified; no failure case analysis
